topic: Induction in a ring of rectangular cross section
problem: A ring of a rectangular cross section (Fig. 203) is made of a material whose resistivity is ρ. The ring is placed in a homogeneous magnetic field. The intensity of the magnetic field is directed along the axis of the ring and increases directly with time, H = kt. Find the intensity of the current induced in the ring.
solution: Divide the ring into thin concentric rings of radius x and width δ. Their circumference is approximated by 2πx and their conducting cross-sectional area is δ h, giving R = ρ (2πx)/(δ h). Use the source-unit Faraday emf proportional to the time rate of flux through radius x, apply Ohm’s law to each thin ring, sum the currents, and take δ → 0.
